purpose: Provide a machine-readable planning view over existing agent workspace, graph builder, and registry state without introducing a new authority.

authorities.verification: explicit verifier entry points such as CompiledGraph.verifyFlat and mathVerifyVectors

invariants: interactionSnapshot and interactionValidActions are read-only projections
no interaction object owns hidden mutable execution state
unknown or parameter-specific conditions remain deferred to the authoritative call boundary
escape hatches remain available and are not removed by the canonical interaction layer

availability_semantics.meaning: available=true means at least one argument assignment can satisfy the known state predicates at snapshot time

phases.workspace_ready: no graph steps and no reserved layer identity is awaiting specification
phases.spec_construction: at least one workspace layer identity is reserved and the graph has no steps
phases.graph_ready: the graph has at least one step and every referenced layer exists in LayerRegistry
phases.graph_incomplete: the graph has at least one step but at least one referenced layer is absent from LayerRegistry

reserveLayerId.effect: reserve metadata identity only; does not initialize execution state

releaseSlot.projection_candidate_policy: only manually reserved slots are suggested; lower-level callers may still use the underlying method directly

workspaceCompile.projection_rule: available when the builder has written outputs and all referenced layers exist in LayerRegistry
workspaceCompile.subject_bound_policy: does not create subject-program binding; a bound-subject graph receipt will fail unless the exact identity was already bound canonically

workspaceBindRuntimeSubject.availability: workspace unbound and canonical runtime layer/slot reservation has not started
workspaceBindRuntimeSubject.effect: bind exact intent/approval/subject/authorization-policy tuple; no LayerRegistry or graph mutation
workspaceBindRuntimeSubject.lifecycle: exact repeat is idempotent; different rebind is rejected

workspaceCompileForRuntimeSubject.authority: AgentGraphBuilder + LayerRegistry compile, then AgentWorkspace exact programIdentity binding
workspaceCompileForRuntimeSubject.availability: runtime subject bound and normal compile candidates exist
workspaceCompileForRuntimeSubject.success: returns CompiledGraph and records exact programIdentity idempotently
workspaceCompileForRuntimeSubject.failure: controlled error with no program-binding mutation; builder/registry remain reusable

conditional_rejoin_actions.workspaceWireUnary: requires an externally initialized layer whose validated init identity exactly matches the supplied AgentLayerSpec
conditional_rejoin_actions.workspaceWireBinary: requires an externally initialized layer whose validated init identity exactly matches the supplied AgentLayerSpec

input_contract.policy: optional; unbound and unknown defer unless shape/layout proves incompatibility

input_port.policy: optional semantic role/provenance metadata for external slot 0; no execution authority

consumer_contract.policy: read-only advisory preflight; consumer requirements are caller-declared, operation choice remains agent authority, and compatibility never authorizes execution

routing_projection.policy: semantic routing is annotation-only; the full canonical interactionValidActions envelope is preserved, candidates remain visible, and graph-step semantics are never inferred from numerical layer type

edge_binding.policy: agent-selected consumer semantics persist on exact graph steps as immutable provenance; binding never changes Burn executable plan identity or authorizes execution

semantic_lifecycle.policy: agent-declared role transitions form immutable provenance chains across graph steps; external lineage is anchored to persistent input edge binding and internal lineage to prior transition fingerprints; no numerical semantics or action authority are introduced

proof_provenance.policy: legacy recordProof, caller attestation, and verifier receipts remain distinct authority classes

resolution_runtime_bridge.policy: bridge transports already-approved/authorized semantic identity; it never chooses runtime actions or grants authority
resolution_runtime_bridge.lifecycle: bind before runtime planning state is reserved; binding is immutable for the workspace lifetime

runtime_resolution_evidence.policy: evidence is classified against the exact Resolution revision + runtime subject; no automatic ResolutionDiagnostic or state transition

math_interaction.role: read-only unified math vocabulary and direct/program binding projection
math_interaction.authority: none beyond catalog binding; operation choice remains agent authority and numerical semantics remain in existing math contracts
math_interaction.valid_operations_role: candidate projection only; selection, ranking, recommendation, execution, and mutation remain outside this surface
math_interaction.binding_plan_role: explicit agent-selected direct|program binding projection; no dispatch, execution, builder mutation, or generation selection
math_interaction.math_proof_role: MathProgram proof plus verifier-owned direct-vs-MathProgramV9 equivalence proof; direct verifier caller supplies neither numerical candidate nor reference

direct_math_verifier.selection_authority: agent remains responsible for choosing the canonical operation; verifier only checks the chosen call
